Most basic dendrogram with R

data <- matrix(sample(seq(1, 2000), 200), ncol = 10)
rownames(data) <- paste0("sample_", seq(1, 20))
colnames(data) <- paste0("variable", seq(1, 10))

# Euclidean distance
dist <- dist(data, diag=TRUE)

# Hierarchical Clustering with hclust
hc <- hclust(dist)

plot(hc)

Zoom on a group

# store the dedrogram in an object
dhc <- as.dendrogram(hc)
plot(dhc[[2]], main = "zoom on a part of the dendrogram")

Dendrogram with color and legend

sample <- paste(rep("sample_",24), seq(1,24), sep="")
specie <- c(rep("dicoccoides", 8), rep("dicoccum", 8), rep("durum", 8))
treatment <- rep(c(rep("High",4 ), rep("Low",4)), 3)
data <- data.frame(sample,specie,treatment)
for (i in seq(1:5)){
  gene <- sample(c(1:40), 24)
  data <- cbind(data, gene)
  colnames(data)[ncol(data)] <- paste("gene_",i,sep="")
 }
data[data$treatment=="High", c(4:8)] <- data[data$treatment=="High", c(4:8)] + 100
data[data$specie=="durum", c(4:8)] <- data[data$specie=="durum", c(4:8)] - 30
rownames(data) <- data[,1]    

head(data)
##            sample      specie treatment gene_1 gene_2 gene_3 gene_4 gene_5
## sample_1 sample_1 dicoccoides      High    124    126    139    139    102
## sample_2 sample_2 dicoccoides      High    130    108    101    131    123
## sample_3 sample_3 dicoccoides      High    129    114    102    107    117
## sample_4 sample_4 dicoccoides      High    117    110    130    137    130
## sample_5 sample_5 dicoccoides       Low     31      7     27     24      7
## sample_6 sample_6 dicoccoides       Low     36     16     12     25     24

dist <- dist(data[, c(4:8)], diag=TRUE)
hc <- hclust(dist)
dhc <- as.dendrogram(hc)

# To color each leaf of the Tree, you have to change the attribute of each leaf.
# This can be done using the dendrapply function. 
i <- 0
colLab <- function(n){
  if(is.leaf(n)){
    a <- attributes(n)
    ligne <- match(attributes(n)$label,data[,1])
    treatment <- data[ligne,3]
    if(treatment=="Low"){col_treatment="blue"}
    if(treatment=="High"){col_treatment="red"}
    specie <- data[ligne,2]
    if(specie=="dicoccoides"){col_specie="red"}
    if(specie=="dicoccum"){col_specie="Darkgreen"}
    if(specie=="durum"){col_specie="blue"}
    
    #Modification of leaf attribute
    attr(n,"nodePar") <- c(a$nodePar,
                           list(cex=1.5,lab.cex=1,pch=20,col=col_treatment,
                                lab.col=col_specie,lab.font=1,lab.cex=1))
  }
  return(n)
}

dL <- dendrapply(dhc, colLab)

plot(dL, main="structure of the population")
legend("topright",legend = c("High Nitrogen", "Low Nitrogen", "Durum", "Dicoccoides", "Dicoccum"), 
     col = c("red", "blue" , "blue" , "red" , "Darkgreen"), 
     pch = c(20,20,4,4,4), bty = "n",  pt.cex = 1.5, cex = 0.8 , 
     text.col = "black", horiz = FALSE, inset = c(0, 0.1))

Customization with dendextend package

Basic dendrogram

library(tidyverse)

mtcars %>% 
  select(mpg, cyl, disp) %>% 
  dist() %>% 
  hclust() %>% 
  as.dendrogram() -> dend
 
par(mar=c(7,3,1,1))
plot(dend)

The set() function

library(dendextend)
par(mar=c(7,3,1,1))
dend %>% set("branches_col", "grey") %>% set("branches_lwd", 3) %>%
  set("labels_col", "orange") %>% set("labels_cex", 0.8) %>% plot()

par(mar=c(7,3,1,1))
dend %>% set("nodes_pch", 19)  %>% set("nodes_cex", 0.7) %>% 
  set("nodes_col", "orange") %>% plot()

par(mar=c(7,3,1,1))
dend %>% set("leaves_pch", 19)  %>% set("leaves_cex", 0.7) %>% 
  set("leaves_col", "skyblue") %>% plot()

Highlight clusters

par(mar=c(7,1,1,1))
dend %>% set("labels_col", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k=3) %>%
  set("branches_k_color", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k = 3) %>% plot(axes=FALSE)

par(mar=c(9,1,1,1))
dend %>% set("labels_col", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k=3) %>%
  set("branches_k_color", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k = 3) %>% plot(axes=FALSE)
rect.dendrogram( dend, k=3, lty = 5, lwd = 0, x=1, col=rgb(0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.1) )

Comparing with an expected clustering

# Create a vector of colors, darkgreen if am is 0, green if 1.
my_colors <- ifelse(mtcars$am==0, "forestgreen", "green")
par(mar=c(10,1,1,1))
dend %>%
  set("labels_col", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k=3) %>%
  set("branches_k_color", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k = 3) %>%
  set("leaves_pch", 19)  %>% set("nodes_cex", 0.7) %>% plot(axes=FALSE)
colored_bars(colors = my_colors, dend = dend, rowLabels = "am")

Comparing 2 dendrograms with tanglegram()

# Make 2 dendrograms, using 2 different clustering methods
d1 <- USArrests %>% dist() %>% hclust( method="average" ) %>% as.dendrogram()
d2 <- USArrests %>% dist() %>% hclust( method="complete" ) %>% as.dendrogram()
 
# Custom these kendo, and place them in a list
dl <- dendlist(
  d1 %>% 
    set("labels_col", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k=3) %>%
    set("branches_lty", 1) %>%
    set("branches_k_color", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k = 3),
  d2 %>% 
    set("labels_col", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k=3) %>%
    set("branches_lty", 1) %>%
    set("branches_k_color", value = c("skyblue", "orange", "grey"), k = 3)
)

tanglegram(dl, common_subtrees_color_lines = FALSE, highlight_distinct_edges = TRUE, 
           highlight_branches_lwd=FALSE, margin_inner=7, lwd=2)
